OMNIPOST - FEATURES AND PIPELINE DOCUMENTATION

OmniPost is a local-first social media post generator. It runs a four stage AI pipeline on a local llama3.2 model through Ollama, with a FastAPI backend and a browser based UI. Everything runs locally, with no external AI services involved.


1. ARCHITECTURE

The browser sends a request to the FastAPI server (app.py, port 8000), which calls the generation engine (model.py). The engine runs the four stage pipeline against Ollama and llama3.2 (port 11434), saves the result to history.json, and returns it to the browser as JSON. The browser also reads history.json through a history endpoint.


2. TECH STACK

Frontend: vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, styled with Inter and JetBrains Mono, using Font Awesome icons.

Backend: FastAPI on Python, calling Ollama's local llama3.2 model through the openai SDK.

Storage: a flat file, history.json, holding the last 100 posts.


4. AI GENERATION PIPELINE

The pipeline runs four stages through llama3.2.

Stage one drafts a strategic plan: key facts from any reference material, a hook suited to the platform, the core message and audience fit, structure and formatting, and a hashtag and call to action strategy.

Stage two writes the first draft based on that plan, grounded in any reference documents, returning only the post text.

Stage three critiques the draft using three parts: Reflect, on hook quality, accuracy, and tone; View, on why the topic matters; and Require, on specific fixes like hook strength, spacing, and length.

Stage four rewrites the post using that critique, following rules on platform fit, factual accuracy, tone, length, emoji count, and formatting, again returning only the final post text.

If deep reflection is turned off, the pipeline stops after stage two and returns that draft as a faster result.


5. OUTPUT SANITIZATION

Before any stage's output is used, it passes through a cleanup function that strips code fences, outer quotation marks, introductory phrases, section labels like Reflect or Require, closing remarks and metadata lines, stray divider lines, and extra blank lines, leaving just the clean post text.

Stage two writes the first draft based on that plan, grounded in any reference documents, returning only the post text.

Stage three critiques the draft using three parts: Reflect, on hook quality, accuracy, and tone; View, on why the topic matters; and Require, on specific fixes like hook strength, spacing, and length.

If deep reflection is turned off, the pipeline stops after stage two and returns that draft as a faster result.

View covers why the topic matters and how to increase its perceived value and engagement. First, it removes code fences, such as triple backtick wrappers.

Second, it removes outer quotation marks if the whole post is wrapped in them.

Third, it removes meta text at the start, such as phrases like "Here is the post," or "Certainly," header labels like a bolded platform name followed by the word Post, field labels like Tone or Subject or Headline, and horizontal rule lines.

Fourth, it applies section cutoffs. Any line that matches a label such as Reflect, View, Require, or Critique causes everything from that line onward to be dropped.

Fifth, it removes meta text at the end, such as sign offs like "Hope this helps," or "Let me know if," along with metadata lines like Character Count, Word Count, or Note.

Sixth, it performs line by line cleanup: internal divider lines made of dashes, equals signs, or asterisks are removed, a leading Hashtags or Tags label is stripped while keeping the tags themselves, blockquote markers are stripped, and consecutive blank lines are collapsed into a single blank line.

Seventh, it trims any leading or trailing empty lines.

The cleaning rules fall into three categories: starting meta patterns, applied from the top of the output; section cutoff patterns, applied as a hard stop anywhere in the output; and ending meta patterns, applied from the bottom of the output.

Posts are saved automatically after every successful generation. They are stored in history.json as a flat JSON list, capped at the 100 most recent entries on a first-in, first-out basis. Each entry keeps the full generation context, so a saved post can be loaded back into the form for editing or regeneration.

Each history entry, and each post returned by the API, includes the following fields.

id: a string UUID that uniquely identifies the post.
created_at: an ISO 8601 timestamp marking when the post was generated.
subject: the post's topic.
tone: the writing tone.
key_message: the core thesis of the post.
target_audience: the intended audience.
length: the length input, for example "150 words."
include_emojis: the emoji setting used.
platform: the lowercase platform key.
platform_name: the platform's display name.
content: the final, sanitized post text.
character_count: the character count of the content.
word_count: the word count of the content.

reflection: the stage three critique output.

LinkedIn allows up to 3,000 characters. Its style guide calls for a professional, thought leadership tone, three to five hashtags, and clear paragraph spacing.

Twitter or X allows up to 280 characters. Its style guide calls for punchy, concise writing with a high impact hook and one to three hashtags.

reference_context: the grounding text supplied by the user.
is_favorite: a true or false flag set by the user.

LinkedIn allows up to 3,000 characters. Its style guide calls for a professional, thought leadership tone, three to five hashtags, and clear paragraph spacing.

Twitter or X allows up to 280 characters. Its style guide calls for punchy, concise writing with a high impact hook and one to three hashtags.

Instagram allows up to 2,200 characters. Its style guide calls for a visual, story driven caption, use of emojis, and hashtags placed at the bottom.

Facebook allows up to 5,000 characters. Its style guide calls for a conversational, community focused tone that starts a discussion.

The project folder, social_media_post_generator, contains the following files.

app.py: the FastAPI server. Handles routing, requests and responses, and history file management.

model.py: the AI pipeline engine. Handles prompt construction, calls to Ollama, output cleaning, and hashtag extraction.

history.json: the persistent flat file post history, created automatically the first time it is needed.

A static folder contains the frontend files: index.html, the single page application markup; style.css, the design system built with CSS custom properties; and app.js, which handles client side state, form handling, API calls, rendering, the history interface, and toast notifications.

# OmniPost — Features & Pipeline Documentation

> **OmniPost** is a local-first social media post generator. It uses a multi-stage AI reasoning pipeline backed by a local `llama3.2` model running through Ollama, exposed via a FastAPI server and a clean browser-based UI.

---

## Table of Contents

1. [Architecture Overview](#1-architecture-overview)
2. [Tech Stack](#2-tech-stack)
3. [Web Interface Features](#3-web-interface-features)
4. [AI Generation Pipeline](#4-ai-generation-pipeline)
5. [Output Sanitization](#5-output-sanitization)
6. [REST API](#6-rest-api)
7. [History & Post Management](#7-history--post-management)
8. [Data Model](#8-data-model)
9. [Platform Specs & Constraints](#9-platform-specs--constraints)
10. [File Map](#10-file-map)

---

## 1. Architecture Overview

```
Browser UI (index.html + app.js)
        │  POST /api/generate
        ▼
FastAPI Server (app.py :8000)
        │
        ▼
Generation Engine (model.py) ── 4-stage prompting ──► Ollama / llama3.2 (:11434)
        │
        ▼
   save to history.json
        │
        ▼
   JSON response ──► Browser
        (Browser also does GET /api/history ──► loads from history.json)
```

The server serves both the static frontend and the REST API from the same process. All generation is 100% local — no external AI services are called.

---

## 2. Tech Stack

| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| **Frontend** | Vanilla HTML, CSS (CSS custom properties), Vanilla JS |
| **Typography** | Inter (body) + JetBrains Mono (code boxes) via Google Fonts |
| **Icons** | Font Awesome 6.5 |
| **Backend** | FastAPI (Python) |
| **AI Runtime** | Ollama (local LLM server) |
| **Model** | `llama3.2` (configurable via `OLLAMA_MODEL` env var) |
| **AI Client** | `openai` Python SDK pointed at Ollama's OpenAI-compatible API |
| **Storage** | `history.json` flat file (last 100 entries, FIFO) |

---

## 3. Web Interface Features

### 3.1 Layout

The UI is a two-column layout:

- **Left column — "Create a Post"**: all generation inputs and controls
- **Right column — "Social Preview & Publishing"**: live post preview card, stats bar, publish/export hub, and generation notes

### 3.2 Input Controls

| Control | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Target Platform** | Button group (4 tabs) | Selects LinkedIn, Twitter/X, Instagram, or Facebook. Updates the preview card theme and character limit hint. |
| **Subject / Topic** | Text input (required) | The main topic of the post. Has a clear (×) button when filled. |
| **Tone** | Text input (freeform) | Writing tone, e.g. *Professional*, *Humorous*, *Bold*. Defaults to `Enthusiastic`. |
| **Reference Documents** | File drop zone + textarea | Drag-and-drop or browse files (`.txt`, `.md`, `.csv`, `.json`). Multiple files are supported. Files are read client-side and concatenated into the reference textarea with `--- [Document: filename] ---` separators. Can also be pasted directly as text. |
| **Key Message / Main Point** | Textarea | The single core insight the post should communicate. |
| **Target Audience** | Text input | Who the post is written for. Defaults to `General Audience`. |
| **Length (Words)** | Number input | Target word count. Range 20–1000, step 10. Defaults to `150`. Sent to the API as `"N words"`. |
| **Include Emojis** | Binary toggle switch | Checked → `engaging` (3–6 emojis). Unchecked → `none` (plain text only). |
| **Generate button** | Submit | Triggers the full 4-stage pipeline. Shows a spinner and cycling stage labels while loading. |

### 3.3 Live Preview Card

After generation, the right column updates with:

- **Platform-styled mockup card** — Visual frame that mimics the target platform's card design (colours, avatar, handle, bio, engagement buttons).
- **Hashtag highlighting** — All `#tags` in the post are highlighted as styled inline badges.
- **Stats bar** — Shows live character count (with a warning colour if over the platform limit), word count, and hashtag count.

### 3.4 Publish / Export Hub

| Action | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| **Copy Post** | Copies the raw post text to the clipboard. |
| **Post to X** | Opens `twitter.com/intent/tweet` with the post pre-filled. |
| **Share to LinkedIn** | Opens LinkedIn share intent with the post pre-filled. |
| **Post to Facebook** | Opens Facebook share dialog with the post pre-filled. |
| **Download .txt** | Downloads the post as `post_{platform}_{timestamp}.txt`. |

### 3.5 Generation Notes (Collapsible Drawer)

After generation, a collapsible "View generation notes" accordion appears with two read-only sections:

- **Notes & self-review** — The AI's self-critique output from Stage 3 (Reflect / View / Require).
- **Drafting plan** — The Chain-of-Thought strategy from Stage 1.

### 3.6 History Drawer

A slide-out drawer (accessible from the "History" button in the header) shows all previously generated posts. Features:

- **Live count badge** on the header button
- **Search** — Filters by subject, content, or tone in real time
- **Platform filter tabs** — All / LinkedIn / X / Instagram
- **Per-item actions** — Copy, Load (populates form + preview), Delete

---

## 4. AI Generation Pipeline

The pipeline runs in four sequential stages, all calling the local `llama3.2` model via Ollama.

```
User Inputs

    ▼
Stage 1 · Chain-of-Thought Strategic Planning     (max_tokens=600, temp=0.7)
    Output: cot_instructions
    │
    ▼
Stage 2 · Initial Draft — Platform Copywriting    (max_tokens=700, temp=0.7)
    Output: draft_content
    │
    │── deep_reflection=False ──► sanitize ──► return (fast mode)
    │
    ▼
Stage 3 · Reflect / View / Require Self-Critique  (max_tokens=500, temp=0.7)
    Output: reflect_content
    │
    ▼
Stage 4 · Refined Final Polish                    (max_tokens=800, temp=0.7)
    Output: final_post
    │
    ▼
sanitize_post_output() → extract_hashtags() → API Response

### Stage 1 — Chain-of-Thought Planning

**Prompt role**: Elite content strategist

Instructs the model to produce a step-by-step strategic plan covering:

1. Extraction of key facts from reference documents
2. Identification of the scroll-stopping hook for the platform
3. Core components and key message for the target audience
4. Structural flow and formatting tailored to the platform
5. CTA and relevant hashtag strategy
6. Tone authenticity and emoji adherence

**Context injected**: subject, tone, key message, target audience, platform name, length guideline, emoji guideline, platform style guide, reference documents (if any).

### Stage 2 — Initial Draft

**Prompt role**: Expert platform copywriter

Takes the Stage 1 plan as strategic instructions and generates the full post. Instructed to output *only* the post text — no introductory notes or meta-commentary. All reference documents are re-injected here for factual grounding.

### Stage 3 — Reflect / View / Require Analysis

**Prompt role**: Critic/analyst

Performs structured self-critique on the Stage 2 draft using three mandatory sections:

| Section | Purpose |

| **Reflect** | Hook quality, key takeaway, factual accuracy vs. reference docs, tone & audience alignment |
| **View** | Why the topic matters; how to elevate perceived value and engagement |
| **Require** | Specific tactical improvements: hook punch, whitespace, CTA strength, emoji count, character limit |

### Stage 4 — Refined Final Polish

**Prompt role**: Master copywriter and editor

Takes the original draft + the Stage 3 critique and produces the final post. Mandatory rules injected into the prompt:

1. Deliver the final post optimized for the platform
2. Factual accuracy from reference documents
3. Preserve tone and speak to target audience
4. Respect length guideline and platform character limit
5. Meet the emoji requirement exactly
6. Clean paragraph breaks for mobile readability
7. No meta-text (`Reflect:`, `View:`, `Require:`, etc.)
8. Return *only* the post text

| **7. Final trim** | Leading and trailing empty lines removed |

- `SECTION_CUTOFF_PATTERNS` — applied as a hard cutoff anywhere in the output
- `END_META_PATTERNS` — applied from the bottom of the output

# OmniPost — Features & Pipeline Documentation

> **OmniPost** is a local-first social media post generator. It uses a multi-stage AI reasoning pipeline backed by a local `llama3.2` model running through Ollama, exposed via a FastAPI server and a clean browser-based UI.

---

## Table of Contents

1. [Architecture Overview](#1-architecture-overview)
2. [Tech Stack](#2-tech-stack)
3. [Web Interface Features](#3-web-interface-features)
4. [AI Generation Pipeline](#4-ai-generation-pipeline)
5. [Output Sanitization](#5-output-sanitization)
6. [REST API](#6-rest-api)
7. [History & Post Management](#7-history--post-management)
8. [Data Model](#8-data-model)
9. [Platform Specs & Constraints](#9-platform-specs--constraints)
10. [File Map](#10-file-map)

---

## 1. Architecture Overview

```
Browser UI (index.html + app.js)
        │  POST /api/generate
        ▼
FastAPI Server (app.py :8000)
        │
        ▼
Generation Engine (model.py) ── 4-stage prompting ──► Ollama / llama3.2 (:11434)
        │
        ▼
   save to history.json
        │
        ▼
   JSON response ──► Browser
        (Browser also does GET /api/history ──► loads from history.json)
```

The server serves both the static frontend and the REST API from the same process. All generation is 100% local — no external AI services are called.

---

## 2. Tech Stack

| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| **Frontend** | Vanilla HTML, CSS (CSS custom properties), Vanilla JS |
| **Typography** | Inter (body) + JetBrains Mono (code boxes) via Google Fonts |
| **Icons** | Font Awesome 6.5 |
| **Backend** | FastAPI (Python) |
| **AI Runtime** | Ollama (local LLM server) |
| **Model** | `llama3.2` (configurable via `OLLAMA_MODEL` env var) |
| **AI Client** | `openai` Python SDK pointed at Ollama's OpenAI-compatible API |
| **Storage** | `history.json` flat file (last 100 entries, FIFO) |

---

## 3. Web Interface Features

### 3.1 Layout

The UI is a two-column layout:

- **Left column — "Create a Post"**: all generation inputs and controls
- **Right column — "Social Preview & Publishing"**: live post preview card, stats bar, publish/export hub, and generation notes

### 3.2 Input Controls

| Control | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Target Platform** | Button group (4 tabs) | Selects LinkedIn, Twitter/X, Instagram, or Facebook. Updates the preview card theme and character limit hint. |
| **Subject / Topic** | Text input (required) | The main topic of the post. Has a clear (×) button when filled. |
| **Tone** | Text input (freeform) | Writing tone, e.g. *Professional*, *Humorous*, *Bold*. Defaults to `Enthusiastic`. |
| **Reference Documents** | File drop zone + textarea | Drag-and-drop or browse files (`.txt`, `.md`, `.csv`, `.json`). Multiple files are supported. Files are read client-side and concatenated into the reference textarea with `--- [Document: filename] ---` separators. Can also be pasted directly as text. |
| **Key Message / Main Point** | Textarea | The single core insight the post should communicate. |
| **Target Audience** | Text input | Who the post is written for. Defaults to `General Audience`. |
| **Length (Words)** | Number input | Target word count. Range 20–1000, step 10. Defaults to `150`. Sent to the API as `"N words"`. |
| **Include Emojis** | Binary toggle switch | Checked → `engaging` (3–6 emojis). Unchecked → `none` (plain text only). |
| **Generate button** | Submit | Triggers the full 4-stage pipeline. Shows a spinner and cycling stage labels while loading. |

### 3.3 Live Preview Card

After generation, the right column updates with:

- **Platform-styled mockup card** — Visual frame that mimics the target platform's card design (colours, avatar, handle, bio, engagement buttons).
- **Hashtag highlighting** — All `#tags` in the post are highlighted as styled inline badges.
- **Stats bar** — Shows live character count (with a warning colour if over the platform limit), word count, and hashtag count.

### 3.4 Publish / Export Hub

| Action | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| **Copy Post** | Copies the raw post text to the clipboard. |
| **Post to X** | Opens `twitter.com/intent/tweet` with the post pre-filled. |
| **Share to LinkedIn** | Opens LinkedIn share intent with the post pre-filled. |
| **Post to Facebook** | Opens Facebook share dialog with the post pre-filled. |
| **Download .txt** | Downloads the post as `post_{platform}_{timestamp}.txt`. |

### 3.5 Generation Notes (Collapsible Drawer)

After generation, a collapsible "View generation notes" accordion appears with two read-only sections:

- **Notes & self-review** — The AI's self-critique output from Stage 3 (Reflect / View / Require).
- **Drafting plan** — The Chain-of-Thought strategy from Stage 1.

### 3.6 History Drawer

A slide-out drawer (accessible from the "History" button in the header) shows all previously generated posts. Features:

- **Live count badge** on the header button
- **Search** — Filters by subject, content, or tone in real time
- **Platform filter tabs** — All / LinkedIn / X / Instagram
- **Per-item actions** — Copy, Load (populates form + preview), Delete

---

## 4. AI Generation Pipeline

The pipeline runs in four sequential stages, all calling the local `llama3.2` model via Ollama.

```
User Inputs
    │
    ▼
Stage 1 · Chain-of-Thought Strategic Planning     (max_tokens=600, temp=0.7)
    Output: cot_instructions
    │
    ▼
Stage 2 · Initial Draft — Platform Copywriting    (max_tokens=700, temp=0.7)
    Output: draft_content
    │
    │── deep_reflection=False ──► sanitize ──► return (fast mode)
    │
    ▼
Stage 3 · Reflect / View / Require Self-Critique  (max_tokens=500, temp=0.7)
    Output: reflect_content
    │
    ▼
Stage 4 · Refined Final Polish                    (max_tokens=800, temp=0.7)
    Output: final_post
    │
    ▼
sanitize_post_output() → extract_hashtags() → API Response
```

### Stage 1 — Chain-of-Thought Planning

**Prompt role**: Elite content strategist

Instructs the model to produce a step-by-step strategic plan covering:

1. Extraction of key facts from reference documents
2. Identification of the scroll-stopping hook for the platform
3. Core components and key message for the target audience
4. Structural flow and formatting tailored to the platform
5. CTA and relevant hashtag strategy
6. Tone authenticity and emoji adherence

**Context injected**: subject, tone, key message, target audience, platform name, length guideline, emoji guideline, platform style guide, reference documents (if any).

### Stage 2 — Initial Draft

**Prompt role**: Expert platform copywriter

Takes the Stage 1 plan as strategic instructions and generates the full post. Instructed to output *only* the post text — no introductory notes or meta-commentary. All reference documents are re-injected here for factual grounding.

### Stage 3 — Reflect / View / Require Analysis

**Prompt role**: Critic/analyst

Performs structured self-critique on the Stage 2 draft using three mandatory sections:

| Section | Purpose |
|---|---|
| **Reflect** | Hook quality, key takeaway, factual accuracy vs. reference docs, tone & audience alignment |
| **View** | Why the topic matters; how to elevate perceived value and engagement |
| **Require** | Specific tactical improvements: hook punch, whitespace, CTA strength, emoji count, character limit |

### Stage 4 — Refined Final Polish

**Prompt role**: Master copywriter and editor

Takes the original draft + the Stage 3 critique and produces the final post. Mandatory rules injected into the prompt:

1. Deliver the final post optimized for the platform
2. Factual accuracy from reference documents
3. Preserve tone and speak to target audience
4. Respect length guideline and platform character limit
5. Meet the emoji requirement exactly
6. Clean paragraph breaks for mobile readability
7. No meta-text (`Reflect:`, `View:`, `Require:`, etc.)
8. Return *only* the post text

---

## 5. Output Sanitization

`sanitize_post_output()` in `model.py` is applied to every stage output before it is returned. It performs 7 cleaning passes in order:

| Pass | What it removes |
|---|---|
| **1. Code fences** | ` ```markdown ... ``` ` or ` ``` ... ``` ` wrappers |
| **2. Outer quotes** | Post wrapped in `"..."` or `'...'` |
| **3. Starting meta lines** | Intro phrases: *"Here is the post:"*, *"Certainly!"*, header labels like `**LinkedIn Post:**`, field labels like `Tone:`, `Subject:`, `Headline:`, horizontal rules |
| **4. Section cutoffs** | Any line matching `Reflect:`, `View:`, `Require:`, `Critique:` etc. — everything from that line onward is dropped |
| **5. Ending meta lines** | Sign-offs: *"Hope this helps!"*, *"Let me know if…"*, metadata lines: `Character count:`, `Word count:`, `Note:` |
| **6. Line-by-line cleanup** | Internal `---` / `===` / `***` dividers removed; `Hashtags:` / `Tags:` prefix stripped (tags kept); blockquote `>` markers stripped; consecutive blank lines collapsed to a single blank line |
| **7. Final trim** | Leading and trailing empty lines removed |

Pattern categories:

- `START_META_PATTERNS` — applied from the top of the output
- `SECTION_CUTOFF_PATTERNS` — applied as a hard cutoff anywhere in the output
- `END_META_PATTERNS` — applied from the bottom of the output

---

## 6. REST API

Base URL: `http://localhost:8000`

### `POST /api/generate`

Triggers the full AI pipeline.

**Request body** (`application/json`):

```
{
  "subject": "AI Agents in 2026",          // required
  "tone": "Enthusiastic",
  "key_message": "...",
  "target_audience": "Tech founders",
  "length": "150 words",                   // "N words" or preset: short/medium/long
  "include_emojis": "engaging",            // "engaging" | "none" | "minimal" | "expressive"
  "platform": "linkedin",                  // linkedin | twitter | instagram | facebook
  "deep_reflection": true,                 // false = fast mode (skip stages 3 & 4)
  "reference_context": "..."               // optional grounding text
}
```

**Response**:

```
{
  "success": true,
  "post": {
    "id": "uuid",
    "created_at": "ISO-8601",
    "subject": "...",
    "tone": "...",
    "key_message": "...",
    "target_audience": "...",
    "length": "...",
    "include_emojis": "...",
    "platform": "linkedin",
    "platform_name": "LinkedIn",
    "content": "final sanitized post text",
    "character_count": 812,
    "word_count": 107,
    "hashtags": ["#AI", "#Tech"],
    "reflection": "Reflect:\n...\nView:\n...\nRequire:\n...",
    "cot_plan": "Chain-of-thought strategy...",
    "reference_context": "...",
    "is_favorite": false
  }
}
```

### `GET /api/history`

Returns stored posts. Supports optional query params:

- `?search=keyword` — filters by subject, content, or tone
- `?platform=linkedin` — filters by platform

### `POST /api/history/{id}/toggle-favorite`

Toggles the `is_favorite` flag for a history item.

### `DELETE /api/history/{id}`

Deletes a single history item.

### `DELETE /api/history`

Clears all history.

---

## 7. History & Post Management

- Posts are saved automatically on every successful generation
- Stored in `history.json` as a flat JSON array
- Capped at **100 most recent entries** (FIFO eviction)
- Each entry stores the full generation context so posts can be loaded back into the UI for re-editing or re-generation

---

## 8. Data Model

Each history entry / API response post object:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `string` (UUID) | Unique identifier |
| `created_at` | `string` (ISO-8601) | Generation timestamp |
| `subject` | `string` | Post topic |
| `tone` | `string` | Writing tone |
| `key_message` | `string` | Core thesis |
| `target_audience` | `string` | Intended audience |
| `length` | `string` | Length input (e.g. `"150 words"`) |
| `include_emojis` | `string` | Emoji setting |
| `platform` | `string` | Platform key (lowercase) |
| `platform_name` | `string` | Platform display name |
| `content` | `string` | Final sanitized post text |
| `character_count` | `int` | Character count of `content` |
| `word_count` | `int` | Word count of `content` |
| `hashtags` | `string[]` | Unique hashtags extracted from `content` |
| `reflection` | `string` | Stage 3 critique output |
| `cot_plan` | `string` | Stage 1 chain-of-thought plan |
| `reference_context` | `string` | Grounding text supplied by user |
| `is_favorite` | `bool` | User-toggled favorite flag |

---

## 9. Platform Specs & Constraints

| Platform | Char Limit | Style Guide |
|---|---|---|
| **LinkedIn** | 3,000 | Professional, thought leadership, 3–5 hashtags, clear paragraph spacing |
| **Twitter / X** | 280 | Punchy, concise, high-impact hook, 1–3 hashtags |
| **Instagram** | 2,200 | Visual caption, storytelling, emojis, hashtags at bottom |
| **Facebook** | 5,000 | Conversational, community-focused, discussion starter |

Character limit is enforced at the prompt level (injected into Stages 2 and 4) and surfaced as a visual warning in the UI stats bar.

---

## 10. File Map

```
social_media_post_generator/
├── app.py              FastAPI server, REST endpoints, history I/O
├── model.py            AI pipeline engine, sanitization, hashtag extraction
├── history.json        Persistent flat-file post history (auto-created)
└── static/
    ├── index.html      Single-page app markup
    ├── style.css       Vanilla CSS design system (CSS custom properties)
    └── app.js          Frontend state management, API calls, UI rendering
```

| File | Responsibility |

| `app.py` | HTTP layer: routing, request/response, CORS, history file management |
| `model.py` | AI layer: prompt construction, Ollama calls, output cleaning, hashtag extraction |
| `index.html` | Semantic HTML structure, form controls, mockup card, history drawer |
| `style.css` | Design tokens, layout, component styles, light editorial theme |
| `app.js` | Client state, form handling, fetch calls, rendering, history UI, toast notifications |

## 1. Architecture Overview

```
Browser UI (index.html + app.js)
        │  POST /api/generate
        ▼
FastAPI Server (app.py :8000)
        │
        ▼
Generation Engine (model.py) ── 4-stage prompting ──► Ollama / llama3.2 (:11434)
        │
        ▼
   save to history.json
        │
        ▼
   JSON response ──► Browser
        (Browser also does GET /api/history ──► loads from history.json)
```

The server serves both the static frontend and the REST API from the same process. All generation is 100% local — no external AI services are called.

---

## 2. Tech Stack

| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| **Frontend** | Vanilla HTML, CSS (CSS custom properties), Vanilla JS |
| **Typography** | Inter (body) + JetBrains Mono (code boxes) via Google Fonts |
| **Icons** | Font Awesome 6.5 |
| **Backend** | FastAPI (Python) |
| **AI Runtime** | Ollama (local LLM server) |
| **Model** | `llama3.2` (configurable via `OLLAMA_MODEL` env var) |
| **AI Client** | `openai` Python SDK pointed at Ollama's OpenAI-compatible API |
| **Storage** | `history.json` flat file (last 100 entries, FIFO) |

---

## 3. Web Interface Features

### 3.1 Layout

The UI is a two-column layout:

- **Left column — "Create a Post"**: all generation inputs and controls
- **Right column — "Social Preview & Publishing"**: live post preview card, stats bar, publish/export hub, and generation notes

### 3.2 Input Controls

| Control | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Target Platform** | Button group (4 tabs) | Selects LinkedIn, Twitter/X, Instagram, or Facebook. Updates the preview card theme and character limit hint. |
| **Subject / Topic** | Text input (required) | The main topic of the post. Has a clear (×) button when filled. |
| **Tone** | Text input (freeform) | Writing tone, e.g. *Professional*, *Humorous*, *Bold*. Defaults to `Enthusiastic`. |
| **Reference Documents** | File drop zone + textarea | Drag-and-drop or browse files (`.txt`, `.md`, `.csv`, `.json`). Multiple files are supported. Files are read client-side and concatenated into the reference textarea with `--- [Document: filename] ---` separators. Can also be pasted directly as text. |
| **Key Message / Main Point** | Textarea | The single core insight the post should communicate. |
| **Target Audience** | Text input | Who the post is written for. Defaults to `General Audience`. |
| **Length (Words)** | Number input | Target word count. Range 20–1000, step 10. Defaults to `150`. Sent to the API as `"N words"`. |
| **Include Emojis** | Binary toggle switch | Checked → `engaging` (3–6 emojis). Unchecked → `none` (plain text only). |
| **Generate button** | Submit | Triggers the full 4-stage pipeline. Shows a spinner and cycling stage labels while loading. |

### 3.3 Live Preview Card

After generation, the right column updates with:

- **Platform-styled mockup card** — Visual frame that mimics the target platform's card design (colours, avatar, handle, bio, engagement buttons).
- **Hashtag highlighting** — All `#tags` in the post are highlighted as styled inline badges.
- **Stats bar** — Shows live character count (with a warning colour if over the platform limit), word count, and hashtag count.

### 3.4 Publish / Export Hub

| Action | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| **Copy Post** | Copies the raw post text to the clipboard. |
| **Post to X** | Opens `twitter.com/intent/tweet` with the post pre-filled. |
| **Share to LinkedIn** | Opens LinkedIn share intent with the post pre-filled. |
| **Post to Facebook** | Opens Facebook share dialog with the post pre-filled. |
| **Download .txt** | Downloads the post as `post_{platform}_{timestamp}.txt`. |

### 3.5 Generation Notes (Collapsible Drawer)

After generation, a collapsible "View generation notes" accordion appears with two read-only sections:

- **Notes & self-review** — The AI's self-critique output from Stage 3 (Reflect / View / Require).
- **Drafting plan** — The Chain-of-Thought strategy from Stage 1.

### 3.6 History Drawer

A slide-out drawer (accessible from the "History" button in the header) shows all previously generated posts. Features:

- **Live count badge** on the header button
- **Search** — Filters by subject, content, or tone in real time
- **Platform filter tabs** — All / LinkedIn / X / Instagram
- **Per-item actions** — Copy, Load (populates form + preview), Delete

---

## 4. AI Generation Pipeline

The pipeline runs in four sequential stages, all calling the local `llama3.2` model via Ollama.

```
User Inputs
    │
    ▼
Stage 1 · Chain-of-Thought Strategic Planning     (max_tokens=600, temp=0.7)
    Output: cot_instructions
    │
    ▼
Stage 2 · Initial Draft — Platform Copywriting    (max_tokens=700, temp=0.7)
    Output: draft_content
    │
    │── deep_reflection=False ──► sanitize ──► return (fast mode)
    │
    ▼
Stage 3 · Reflect / View / Require Self-Critique  (max_tokens=500, temp=0.7)
    Output: reflect_content
    │
    ▼
Stage 4 · Refined Final Polish                    (max_tokens=800, temp=0.7)
    Output: final_post
    │
    ▼
sanitize_post_output() → extract_hashtags() → API Response
```

### Stage 1 — Chain-of-Thought Planning

**Prompt role**: Elite content strategist

Instructs the model to produce a step-by-step strategic plan covering:

1. Extraction of key facts from reference documents
2. Identification of the scroll-stopping hook for the platform
3. Core components and key message for the target audience
4. Structural flow and formatting tailored to the platform
5. CTA and relevant hashtag strategy
6. Tone authenticity and emoji adherence

**Context injected**: subject, tone, key message, target audience, platform name, length guideline, emoji guideline, platform style guide, reference documents (if any).

### Stage 2 — Initial Draft

**Prompt role**: Expert platform copywriter

Takes the Stage 1 plan as strategic instructions and generates the full post. Instructed to output *only* the post text — no introductory notes or meta-commentary. All reference documents are re-injected here for factual grounding.

### Stage 3 — Reflect / View / Require Analysis

**Prompt role**: Critic/analyst

Performs structured self-critique on the Stage 2 draft using three mandatory sections:

| Section | Purpose |
|---|---|
| **Reflect** | Hook quality, key takeaway, factual accuracy vs. reference docs, tone & audience alignment |
| **View** | Why the topic matters; how to elevate perceived value and engagement |
| **Require** | Specific tactical improvements: hook punch, whitespace, CTA strength, emoji count, character limit |

### Stage 4 — Refined Final Polish

**Prompt role**: Master copywriter and editor

Takes the original draft + the Stage 3 critique and produces the final post. Mandatory rules injected into the prompt:

1. Deliver the final post optimized for the platform
2. Factual accuracy from reference documents
3. Preserve tone and speak to target audience
4. Respect length guideline and platform character limit
5. Meet the emoji requirement exactly
6. Clean paragraph breaks for mobile readability
7. No meta-text (`Reflect:`, `View:`, `Require:`, etc.)
8. Return *only* the post text

---

## 5. Output Sanitization

`sanitize_post_output()` in `model.py` is applied to every stage output before it is returned. It performs 7 cleaning passes in order:

| Pass | What it removes |
|---|---|
| **1. Code fences** | ` ```markdown ... ``` ` or ` ``` ... ``` ` wrappers |
| **2. Outer quotes** | Post wrapped in `"..."` or `'...'` |
| **3. Starting meta lines** | Intro phrases: *"Here is the post:"*, *"Certainly!"*, header labels like `**LinkedIn Post:**`, field labels like `Tone:`, `Subject:`, `Headline:`, horizontal rules |
| **4. Section cutoffs** | Any line matching `Reflect:`, `View:`, `Require:`, `Critique:` etc. — everything from that line onward is dropped |
| **5. Ending meta lines** | Sign-offs: *"Hope this helps!"*, *"Let me know if…"*, metadata lines: `Character count:`, `Word count:`, `Note:` |
| **6. Line-by-line cleanup** | Internal `---` / `===` / `***` dividers removed; `Hashtags:` / `Tags:` prefix stripped (tags kept); blockquote `>` markers stripped; consecutive blank lines collapsed to a single blank line |
| **7. Final trim** | Leading and trailing empty lines removed |

Pattern categories:

- `START_META_PATTERNS` — applied from the top of the output
- `SECTION_CUTOFF_PATTERNS` — applied as a hard cutoff anywhere in the output
- `END_META_PATTERNS` — applied from the bottom of the output

---

## 6. REST API

Base URL: `http://localhost:8000`

### `POST /api/generate`

Triggers the full AI pipeline.

**Request body** (`application/json`):

```
{
  "subject": "AI Agents in 2026",          // required
  "tone": "Enthusiastic",
  "key_message": "...",
  "target_audience": "Tech founders",
  "length": "150 words",                   // "N words" or preset: short/medium/long
  "include_emojis": "engaging",            // "engaging" | "none" | "minimal" | "expressive"
  "platform": "linkedin",                  // linkedin | twitter | instagram | facebook
  "deep_reflection": true,                 // false = fast mode (skip stages 3 & 4)
  "reference_context": "..."               // optional grounding text
}
```

**Response**:

```
{
  "success": true,
  "post": {
    "id": "uuid",
    "created_at": "ISO-8601",
    "subject": "...",
    "tone": "...",
    "key_message": "...",
    "target_audience": "...",
    "length": "...",
    "include_emojis": "...",
    "platform": "linkedin",
    "platform_name": "LinkedIn",
    "content": "final sanitized post text",
    "character_count": 812,
    "word_count": 107,
    "hashtags": ["#AI", "#Tech"],
    "reflection": "Reflect:\n...\nView:\n...\nRequire:\n...",
    "cot_plan": "Chain-of-thought strategy...",
    "reference_context": "...",
    "is_favorite": false
  }
}
```

### `GET /api/history`

Returns stored posts. Supports optional query params:

- `?search=keyword` — filters by subject, content, or tone
- `?platform=linkedin` — filters by platform

### `POST /api/history/{id}/toggle-favorite`

Toggles the `is_favorite` flag for a history item.

### `DELETE /api/history/{id}`

Deletes a single history item.

### `DELETE /api/history`

Clears all history.

---

## 7. History & Post Management

- Posts are saved automatically on every successful generation
- Stored in `history.json` as a flat JSON array
- Capped at **100 most recent entries** (FIFO eviction)
- Each entry stores the full generation context so posts can be loaded back into the UI for re-editing or re-generation

---

## 8. Data Model

Each history entry / API response post object:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `string` (UUID) | Unique identifier |
| `created_at` | `string` (ISO-8601) | Generation timestamp |
| `subject` | `string` | Post topic |
| `tone` | `string` | Writing tone |
| `key_message` | `string` | Core thesis |
| `target_audience` | `string` | Intended audience |
| `length` | `string` | Length input (e.g. `"150 words"`) |
| `include_emojis` | `string` | Emoji setting |
| `platform` | `string` | Platform key (lowercase) |
| `platform_name` | `string` | Platform display name |
| `content` | `string` | Final sanitized post text |
| `character_count` | `int` | Character count of `content` |
| `word_count` | `int` | Word count of `content` |
| `hashtags` | `string[]` | Unique hashtags extracted from `content` |
| `reflection` | `string` | Stage 3 critique output |
| `cot_plan` | `string` | Stage 1 chain-of-thought plan |
| `reference_context` | `string` | Grounding text supplied by user |
| `is_favorite` | `bool` | User-toggled favorite flag |

---

## 9. Platform Specs & Constraints

| Platform | Char Limit | Style Guide |
|---|---|---|
| **LinkedIn** | 3,000 | Professional, thought leadership, 3–5 hashtags, clear paragraph spacing |
| **Twitter / X** | 280 | Punchy, concise, high-impact hook, 1–3 hashtags |
| **Instagram** | 2,200 | Visual caption, storytelling, emojis, hashtags at bottom |
| **Facebook** | 5,000 | Conversational, community-focused, discussion starter |

Character limit is enforced at the prompt level (injected into Stages 2 and 4) and surfaced as a visual warning in the UI stats bar.

---

## 10. File Map

```
social_media_post_generator/
├── app.py              FastAPI server, REST endpoints, history I/O
├── model.py            AI pipeline engine, sanitization, hashtag extraction
├── history.json        Persistent flat-file post history (auto-created)
└── static/
    ├── index.html      Single-page app markup
    ├── style.css       Vanilla CSS design system (CSS custom properties)
    └── app.js          Frontend state management, API calls, UI rendering
```

| File | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `app.py` | HTTP layer: routing, request/response, CORS, history file management |
| `model.py` | AI layer: prompt construction, Ollama calls, output cleaning, hashtag extraction |
| `index.html` | Semantic HTML structure, form controls, mockup card, history drawer |
| `style.css` | Design tokens, layout, component styles, light editorial theme |
| `app.js` | Client state, form handling, fetch calls, rendering, history UI, toast notifications |

```

The server serves both the static frontend and the REST API from the same process. All generation is 100% local — no external AI services are called.

---

## 2. Tech Stack

| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| **Frontend** | Vanilla HTML, CSS (CSS custom properties), Vanilla JS |
| **Typography** | Inter (body) + JetBrains Mono (code boxes) via Google Fonts |
| **Icons** | Font Awesome 6.5 |
| **Backend** | FastAPI (Python) |
| **AI Runtime** | Ollama (local LLM server) |
| **Model** | `llama3.2` (configurable via `OLLAMA_MODEL` env var) |
| **AI Client** | `openai` Python SDK pointed at Ollama's OpenAI-compatible API |
| **Storage** | `history.json` flat file (last 100 entries, FIFO) |

---

## 3. Web Interface Features

### 3.1 Layout

The UI is a two-column layout:

- **Left column — "Create a Post"**: all generation inputs and controls
- **Right column — "Social Preview & Publishing"**: live post preview card, stats bar, publish/export hub, and generation notes

### 3.2 Input Controls

| Control | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Target Platform** | Button group (4 tabs) | Selects LinkedIn, Twitter/X, Instagram, or Facebook. Updates the preview card theme and character limit hint. |
| **Subject / Topic** | Text input (required) | The main topic of the post. Has a clear (×) button when filled. |
| **Tone** | Text input (freeform) | Writing tone, e.g. *Professional*, *Humorous*, *Bold*. Defaults to `Enthusiastic`. |
| **Reference Documents** | File drop zone + textarea | Drag-and-drop or browse files (`.txt`, `.md`, `.csv`, `.json`). Multiple files are supported. Files are read client-side and concatenated into the reference textarea with `--- [Document: filename] ---` separators. Can also be pasted directly as text. |
| **Key Message / Main Point** | Textarea | The single core insight the post should communicate. |
| **Target Audience** | Text input | Who the post is written for. Defaults to `General Audience`. |
| **Length (Words)** | Number input | Target word count. Range 20–1000, step 10. Defaults to `150`. Sent to the API as `"N words"`. |
| **Include Emojis** | Binary toggle switch | Checked → `engaging` (3–6 emojis). Unchecked → `none` (plain text only). |
| **Generate button** | Submit | Triggers the full 4-stage pipeline. Shows a spinner and cycling stage labels while loading. |

### 3.3 Live Preview Card

After generation, the right column updates with:

- **Platform-styled mockup card** — Visual frame that mimics the target platform's card design (colours, avatar, handle, bio, engagement buttons).
- **Hashtag highlighting** — All `#tags` in the post are highlighted as styled inline badges.
- **Stats bar** — Shows live character count (with a warning colour if over the platform limit), word count, and hashtag count.

### 3.4 Publish / Export Hub

| Action | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| **Copy Post** | Copies the raw post text to the clipboard. |
| **Post to X** | Opens `twitter.com/intent/tweet` with the post pre-filled. |
| **Share to LinkedIn** | Opens LinkedIn share intent with the post pre-filled. |
| **Post to Facebook** | Opens Facebook share dialog with the post pre-filled. |
| **Download .txt** | Downloads the post as `post_{platform}_{timestamp}.txt`. |

### 3.5 Generation Notes (Collapsible Drawer)

After generation, a collapsible "View generation notes" accordion appears with two read-only sections:

- **Notes & self-review** — The AI's self-critique output from Stage 3 (Reflect / View / Require).
- **Drafting plan** — The Chain-of-Thought strategy from Stage 1.

### 3.6 History Drawer

A slide-out drawer (accessible from the "History" button in the header) shows all previously generated posts. Features:

- **Live count badge** on the header button
- **Search** — Filters by subject, content, or tone in real time
- **Platform filter tabs** — All / LinkedIn / X / Instagram
- **Per-item actions** — Copy, Load (populates form + preview), Delete

---

## 4. AI Generation Pipeline

The pipeline runs in four sequential stages, all calling the local `llama3.2` model via Ollama.

```
User Inputs
    │
    ▼
Stage 1 · Chain-of-Thought Strategic Planning     (max_tokens=600, temp=0.7)
    Output: cot_instructions
    │
    ▼
Stage 2 · Initial Draft — Platform Copywriting    (max_tokens=700, temp=0.7)
    Output: draft_content
    │
    │── deep_reflection=False ──► sanitize ──► return (fast mode)
    │
    ▼
Stage 3 · Reflect / View / Require Self-Critique  (max_tokens=500, temp=0.7)
    Output: reflect_content
    │
    ▼
Stage 4 · Refined Final Polish                    (max_tokens=800, temp=0.7)
    Output: final_post
    │
    ▼
sanitize_post_output() → extract_hashtags() → API Response
```

### Stage 1 — Chain-of-Thought Planning

**Prompt role**: Elite content strategist

Instructs the model to produce a step-by-step strategic plan covering:

1. Extraction of key facts from reference documents
2. Identification of the scroll-stopping hook for the platform
3. Core components and key message for the target audience
4. Structural flow and formatting tailored to the platform
5. CTA and relevant hashtag strategy
6. Tone authenticity and emoji adherence

**Context injected**: subject, tone, key message, target audience, platform name, length guideline, emoji guideline, platform style guide, reference documents (if any).

### Stage 2 — Initial Draft

**Prompt role**: Expert platform copywriter

Takes the Stage 1 plan as strategic instructions and generates the full post. Instructed to output *only* the post text — no introductory notes or meta-commentary. All reference documents are re-injected here for factual grounding.

### Stage 3 — Reflect / View / Require Analysis

**Prompt role**: Critic/analyst

Performs structured self-critique on the Stage 2 draft using three mandatory sections:

| Section | Purpose |
|---|---|
| **Reflect** | Hook quality, key takeaway, factual accuracy vs. reference docs, tone & audience alignment |
| **View** | Why the topic matters; how to elevate perceived value and engagement |
| **Require** | Specific tactical improvements: hook punch, whitespace, CTA strength, emoji count, character limit |

### Stage 4 — Refined Final Polish

**Prompt role**: Master copywriter and editor

Takes the original draft + the Stage 3 critique and produces the final post. Mandatory rules injected into the prompt:

1. Deliver the final post optimized for the platform
2. Factual accuracy from reference documents
3. Preserve tone and speak to target audience
4. Respect length guideline and platform character limit
5. Meet the emoji requirement exactly
6. Clean paragraph breaks for mobile readability
7. No meta-text (`Reflect:`, `View:`, `Require:`, etc.)
8. Return *only* the post text

---

## 5. Output Sanitization

`sanitize_post_output()` in `model.py` is applied to every stage output before it is returned. It performs 7 cleaning passes in order:

| Pass | What it removes |
|---|---|
| **1. Code fences** | ` ```markdown ... ``` ` or ` ``` ... ``` ` wrappers |
| **2. Outer quotes** | Post wrapped in `"..."` or `'...'` |
| **3. Starting meta lines** | Intro phrases: *"Here is the post:"*, *"Certainly!"*, header labels like `**LinkedIn Post:**`, field labels like `Tone:`, `Subject:`, `Headline:`, horizontal rules |
| **4. Section cutoffs** | Any line matching `Reflect:`, `View:`, `Require:`, `Critique:` etc. — everything from that line onward is dropped |
| **5. Ending meta lines** | Sign-offs: *"Hope this helps!"*, *"Let me know if…"*, metadata lines: `Character count:`, `Word count:`, `Note:` |
| **6. Line-by-line cleanup** | Internal `---` / `===` / `***` dividers removed; `Hashtags:` / `Tags:` prefix stripped (tags kept); blockquote `>` markers stripped; consecutive blank lines collapsed to a single blank line |
| **7. Final trim** | Leading and trailing empty lines removed |

Pattern categories:

- `START_META_PATTERNS` — applied from the top of the output
- `SECTION_CUTOFF_PATTERNS` — applied as a hard cutoff anywhere in the output
- `END_META_PATTERNS` — applied from the bottom of the output

---

## 6. REST API

Base URL: `http://localhost:8000`

### `POST /api/generate`

Triggers the full AI pipeline.

**Request body** (`application/json`):

```
{
  "subject": "AI Agents in 2026",          // required
  "tone": "Enthusiastic",
  "key_message": "...",
  "target_audience": "Tech founders",
  "length": "150 words",                   // "N words" or preset: short/medium/long
  "include_emojis": "engaging",            // "engaging" | "none" | "minimal" | "expressive"
  "platform": "linkedin",                  // linkedin | twitter | instagram | facebook
  "deep_reflection": true,                 // false = fast mode (skip stages 3 & 4)
  "reference_context": "..."               // optional grounding text
}
```

**Response**:

```
{
  "success": true,
  "post": {
    "id": "uuid",
    "created_at": "ISO-8601",
    "subject": "...",
    "tone": "...",
    "key_message": "...",
    "target_audience": "...",
    "length": "...",
    "include_emojis": "...",
    "platform": "linkedin",
    "platform_name": "LinkedIn",
    "content": "final sanitized post text",
    "character_count": 812,
    "word_count": 107,
    "hashtags": ["#AI", "#Tech"],
    "reflection": "Reflect:\n...\nView:\n...\nRequire:\n...",
    "cot_plan": "Chain-of-thought strategy...",
    "reference_context": "...",
    "is_favorite": false
  }
}
```

### `GET /api/history`

Returns stored posts. Supports optional query params:

- `?search=keyword` — filters by subject, content, or tone
- `?platform=linkedin` — filters by platform

### `POST /api/history/{id}/toggle-favorite`

Toggles the `is_favorite` flag for a history item.

### `DELETE /api/history/{id}`

Deletes a single history item.

### `DELETE /api/history`

Clears all history.

---

## 7. History & Post Management

- Posts are saved automatically on every successful generation
- Stored in `history.json` as a flat JSON array
- Capped at **100 most recent entries** (FIFO eviction)
- Each entry stores the full generation context so posts can be loaded back into the UI for re-editing or re-generation

---

## 8. Data Model

Each history entry / API response post object:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `string` (UUID) | Unique identifier |
| `created_at` | `string` (ISO-8601) | Generation timestamp |
| `subject` | `string` | Post topic |
| `tone` | `string` | Writing tone |
| `key_message` | `string` | Core thesis |
| `target_audience` | `string` | Intended audience |
| `length` | `string` | Length input (e.g. `"150 words"`) |
| `include_emojis` | `string` | Emoji setting |
| `platform` | `string` | Platform key (lowercase) |
| `platform_name` | `string` | Platform display name |
| `content` | `string` | Final sanitized post text |
| `character_count` | `int` | Character count of `content` |
| `word_count` | `int` | Word count of `content` |
| `hashtags` | `string[]` | Unique hashtags extracted from `content` |
| `reflection` | `string` | Stage 3 critique output |
| `cot_plan` | `string` | Stage 1 chain-of-thought plan |
| `reference_context` | `string` | Grounding text supplied by user |
| `is_favorite` | `bool` | User-toggled favorite flag |

---

## 9. Platform Specs & Constraints

| Platform | Char Limit | Style Guide |
|---|---|---|
| **LinkedIn** | 3,000 | Professional, thought leadership, 3–5 hashtags, clear paragraph spacing |
| **Twitter / X** | 280 | Punchy, concise, high-impact hook, 1–3 hashtags |
| **Instagram** | 2,200 | Visual caption, storytelling, emojis, hashtags at bottom |
| **Facebook** | 5,000 | Conversational, community-focused, discussion starter |

Character limit is enforced at the prompt level (injected into Stages 2 and 4) and surfaced as a visual warning in the UI stats bar.

---

## 10. File Map

```
social_media_post_generator/
├── app.py              FastAPI server, REST endpoints, history I/O
├── model.py            AI pipeline engine, sanitization, hashtag extraction
├── history.json        Persistent flat-file post history (auto-created)
└── static/
    ├── index.html      Single-page app markup
    ├── style.css       Vanilla CSS design system (CSS custom properties)
    └── app.js          Frontend state management, API calls, UI rendering
```

| File | Responsibility |

| `app.py` | HTTP layer: routing, request/response, CORS, history file management |
| `model.py` | AI layer: prompt construction, Ollama calls, output cleaning, hashtag extraction |

| `style.css` | Design tokens, layout, component styles, light editorial theme |
